'''Leonid Saveliyovych Radvinsky'''{{efn|{{langx|uk|Леонід Савелійович Радвінський|{{transliteration|uk|ukrainian|Leonid Saveliyovych Radvinskyi}}}}}} (May 30, 1982 – March 20, 2026) was an <!-- Do not add "Ukrainian", "Ukrainian-born", etc. per [[MOS:CONTEXTBIO]]. -->American billionaire businessman and the majority owner of [[OnlyFans]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=March 20, 2026 |date=March 20, 2026 |language=en |title=OnlyFans owner Leonid Radvinsky dies at 43 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c33le6yv7pno}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Born in the [[Ukrainian SSR]], Radvinsky was the founder of the cam site [[MyFreeCams]] (through his [[holding company]], MFCXY, Inc.),<ref name="dnb">{{cite web|url=https://www.dnb.com/business-directory/company-profiles.mfcxy_inc.208bac555992f796ec1dff0ab9f258a4.html|access-date=July 2, 2021|title=Mfcxy, Inc. Company Profile|publisher=[[D&B]]}}</ref><ref name="FT">{{cite news |last1=Nilsson |first1=Patricia |title=OnlyFans blurs boundaries as lockdown demand drives success |url=https://www.ft.com/content/f034e311-942e-4d4f-a970-81ee54c568a3 |access-date=May 25, 2021 |work=The Financial Times |date=April 30, 2021}}</ref> and the majority owner of OnlyFans, a [[Subscription business model|content subscription service]] website, mostly used by [[Pornographic film actor|pornographic actresses]] to sell their [[Pornography|pornographic content]]. His website lists his personal investment portfolio.<ref>{{cite web|title=lr.com|url=https://lr.com}}</ref> He had an estimated net worth of $4.7 billion at the time of his death, according to ''[[Forbes]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Conor |date=March 23, 2026 |title=Billionaire OnlyFans Owner Leonid Radvinsky Dies At 43 |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2026/03/23/billionaire-onlyfans-owner-leonid-radvinsky-dies-at-43/ |access-date=March 23, 2026 |website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Radvinsky was born in [[Odesa]] on May 30, 1982, to a [[Jewish]] family.<ref name="nytimes">{{cite web|title=Leon Radvinsky, 43, Dies; Built the Adult-Entertainment Giant OnlyFans|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/25/business/media/leonid-radvinsky-dead.html|date=March 25, 2026|last=Risen|first=Clay|publisher=|access-date=March 25, 2026|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> His family later emigrated to [[Chicago]] when he was a child.<ref name=telegraph>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2022/10/01/elusive-porn-baron-behind-onlyfans/|title=The elusive porn baron behind OnlyFans|newspaper=The Telegraph|author=Matthew Field|date=October 2022 }}</ref> He attended [[Glenbrook South High School]] in [[Glenview, Illinois]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/obituaries/2026/03/23/leo-radvinsky-onlyfans-owner-dead-43-glenview |title=Leo Radvinsky, OnlyFans owner who grew up in Chicago area, dies at 43 |newspaper=Chicago Sun-Times |author=Kade Heather |date=March 23, 2026}}</ref> In 2002, he graduated from [[Northwestern University]] with a degree in economics.<ref name=li1/><ref name=insider>{{cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/onlyfans-owner-leonid-radvinsky-quest-to-join-the-super-rich-2022-10|title=OnlyFans owner Leonid Radvinsky's quest to join the super-rich|publisher=Business Insider|author=Jyoti Mann}}</ref>

==Career==
===Early career===
In 1999, when Radvinsky was 17 years old, he helped incorporate Cybertania Inc., a website referral business.<ref name=telegraph/> During the late 1990s and early 2000s, Radvinsky developed more than ten websites such as Password Universe, Working Passes, and Ultra Passwords that claimed and were advertised to provide users with "illegal" and "hacked" [[Password cracking|passwords]] to porn sites, where he earned money for every click;<ref name=telegraph/><ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Brewster |first1=Thomas |last2=Dawkins |first2=David |title=The Shady, Secret History Of OnlyFans' Billionaire Owner |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/thomasbrewster/2021/06/16/the-shady-secret-history-of-onlyfans-billionaire-owner/ |access-date=June 20, 2021 |work=[[Forbes]] |date=June 16, 2021}}</ref> one of the involved websites advertised more than 10,000 "illegal pre-teen passwords".<ref name=insider/> However, according to ''[[Forbes]]'', there was not any evidence suggesting the sites actually linked to illegal content.<ref name=":0" /> Ultra Passwords reportedly earned $1.8 million a year in revenue during the 2000s.<ref name=insider/>

In 2004, Radvinsky founded [[MyFreeCams]], an adult streaming website.<ref name=telegraph/> The same year, [[Microsoft]] sued Radvinsky for allegedly sending millions of deceptive emails to [[Hotmail]] users, but the case was eventually dismissed.<ref name="Bloomberg LP">{{cite news |last1=Shaw |first1=Lucas |title=OnlyFans Is a Billion-Dollar Media Giant Hiding in Plain Sight |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-12-05/celebrities-like-cardi-b-could-turn-onlyfans-into-a-billion-dollar-media-company |access-date=May 25, 2021 |work=Bloomberg LP |date=December 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Microsoft]]|date=September 28, 2004|access-date=July 2, 2021|title=Amazon.com, Microsoft Team Against Online Fraud|url=https://news.microsoft.com/2004/09/28/amazon-com-microsoft-team-against-online-fraud/|quote=Microsoft, too, filed a new and separate [[lawsuit]] against Leonid ("Leo") Radvinsky and his Chicago-based businesses Activsoft, Inc., and Cybertania, Inc.}}</ref>

===Venture capital===
Radvinsky operated a [[venture capital]] fund called "Leo", founded in 2009,<ref name="li1">{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2026 |title=OnlyFans owner Leonid Radvinsky dies of cancer at 43 - CBS News |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/leonid-radvinsky-onlyfans-owner-cancer-death-age-43/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260325054026/https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/onlyfans-owner-leonid-radvinsky-dies-cancer-43-bloomberg-news-reports-2026-03-23/ |archive-date=March 25, 2026 |access-date=March 26, 2026 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref> which invests mainly in [[tech companies]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Leo.com|title=Leo.com|url=https://leo.com|access-date=June 11, 2021}}</ref> The fund's notable investments include Israel-based B4X and the social networking software [[Pleroma (software)|Pleroma]].<ref name="insider" /> 

===OnlyFans===
In 2018, Radvinsky bought a 75% stake in [[OnlyFans]]' parent company Fenix International Ltd. from its British founders [[Tim Stokely]] and his father [[Guy Stokely]].<ref name="FT"/><ref name="The Independent">{{cite news |last1=Zitser |first1=Joshua |title='Being made homeless is a perpetual fear': What it's like to risk everything just for posting on OnlyFans |url=https://www.indy100.com/people/onlyfans-lauren-kwei-sex-work-b1777617 |access-date=May 25, 2021 |work=[[The Independent]] |date=December 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=August 27, 2023 |title=OnlyFans: Who is Leonid Radvinsky, the elusive owner of a porn empire? |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-66615008 |access-date=September 21, 2023}}</ref> After this, OnlyFans became increasingly focused on [[not safe for work]] (NSFW) content and "gained a pop culture reputation for being a hive of pornography".<ref name="The Independent"/> OnlyFans had annual revenues in excess of $6.6{{nbsp}}billion as of November 2023, with revenues growing 19% per year.<ref name="find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk">{{cite web |title=Fenix International Limited – Filing History |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/10354575/filing-history |website=GOV.UK |access-date=September 11, 2024}}</ref> Radvinsky received $472{{nbsp}}million in dividends from the website in 2023, up from $338{{nbsp}}million and $284{{nbsp}}million in 2022 and 2021, respectively.<ref name="find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk"/> Radvinsky was paid $701 million by OnlyFans in 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 23, 2026 |title=Leonid Radvinsky, owner of OnlyFans, dies aged 43 |last1=Dowell|first1=Anna|language=en-GB |work=The Times |url=https://www.thetimes.com/us/news-today/article/leo-radvinsky-onlyfans-dies-98b09k7gt}}</ref>

===Philanthropy===
In 2024, Radvinsky and his wife were both major public supporters of a $23 million grant program for cancer research, which was announced at a [[gastrointestinal]] research foundation gala.<ref name="WSJ" /> He donated $5 million to [[Ukraine]] relief in 2022 as well as a cancer charity, an animal-welfare organization, and a skin-disorder-research fund.<ref name="insider" /> Radvinsky also donated to the [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center]] and the West Suburban Humane Society.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adebayo |first=Ademide |date=March 23, 2026 |title=OnlyFans Owner Leonid Radvinsky Dies At 43 |url=https://www.arise.tv/onlyfans-owner-leonid-radvinsky-dies-at-43/ |access-date=March 23, 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Radvinsky indicated on his personal website his aspiration to sign [[The Giving Pledge]], a public commitment by wealthy individuals to donate the majority of their fortune to philanthropic causes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Giving |url=https://leoradvinsky.com/giving |access-date=August 19, 2025 |website=Giving |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Radvinsky was married to Yekaterina "Katie" Chudnovsky, an attorney and philanthropist. Radvinsky married Yekaterina in 2008, they have four children.<ref>Patrick Kidd: [https://observer.co.uk/profile/obituary/article/leonid-radvinsky-onlyfans-owner ''Obituary: Leonid Radvinsky, OnlyFans owner.''] In: ''[[The Observer]]'', 26. März 2026 (englisch).</ref> He led a private life and only a few photos of him appear to exist. Radvinsky's website<ref>{{cite web|title=lr.com|url=https://lr.com}}</ref> does not mention OnlyFans but lists his investments in open source software.<ref name="nytimes" /> Later in his life, Radvinsky became a [[recluse]] and lived in a $19 million, 6,000-square-foot ({{convert|6,000|ft2|m2|disp=out}}) oceanfront condo in the [[Miami]] area.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2026 |title=OnlyFans owner, a recluse with one photo, died days before news broke |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/onlyfans-leonid-radvinsky-cause-death-health-family-b2945147.html |access-date=March 26, 2026 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

Radvinsky's website states, "A first-generation immigrant from Ukraine, technology was imprinted on Leo at an early age while gaming with BASIC on his grandfather's [[I386|i386 PC]]. Leo went on to study economics at Northwestern University, where high marks led him to become class valedictorian. In his downtime, Leo is an avid reader who’s always ready for a chess match and is an aspiring helicopter pilot. He currently resides in sunny Florida."<ref>{{Cite web |title=ABOUT |url=https://www.lr.com/about-leo-radvinsky |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Leo Radvinsky |language=en}}</ref>

===Political activity===
In 2023, according to ''[[The Lever]]''{{'}}s reporting on confidential internal documents obtained from [[AIPAC]]—a [[pro-Israel]] [[Israel lobby in the United States|lobbying group]]—Radvinsky and his wife had contributed $11{{nbsp}}million to the organization. When emailed for comment, AIPAC strongly condemned the report, and Radvinsky denied his contribution, writing "I don't know" when asked why his name appeared in the documentation. ''The Lever'' also reported the existence of a documented [[wire transfer]] from Radvinsky's wife to the organization.<ref name="TheLever">{{cite web |last1=Barshad |first1=Amos |title=Inside The Israel Lobby's New $90 Million War Chest |url=https://www.levernews.com/inside-the-israel-lobbys-new-90-million-war-chest/ |website=The Lever |access-date=March 29, 2024}}</ref>

===Technology===
Radvinsky was a supporter of the [[Elixir (programming language)|Elixir]] programming language.<ref name="lr1">{{cite web|url=https://www.lr.com/about-leo-radvinsky|title=About|first=Leonid|last=Radvinsky|quote=A first-generation immigrant from [[Ukraine]], technology was imprinted on Leo at an early age|access-date=June 11, 2021}}</ref>

==Death==
Radvinsky died on March 20, 2026, at the age of 43,<ref name=vlessing>{{cite web | url= https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/onlyfans-owner-leonid-radvinsky-dead-1236544306/ | title= OnlyFans owner Leonid Radvinsky dies of cancer at 43 | date= March 23, 2026 | access-date= March 23, 2026 | work= The Hollywood Reporter (via Reuters) | author = Etan Vlessing | quote= OnlyFans said in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter on Monday after Radvinsky’s death on March 20. |language= en }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> following a long period of cancer previously kept secret.<ref name=":1">{{cite news |title=Secretive billionaire owner of OnlyFans dies at 43 |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/business/article/onlyfans-owner-leonid-radvinsky-dies-at-43/ |access-date=March 23, 2026 |work=Reuters |agency=CTV News |date=March 23, 2026}}</ref> OnlyFans released a statement announcing his death on March 23, saying they were "deeply saddened" by the news.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2026 |last=Lamba |first=Kritika |title=Leonid Radvinsky death: OnlyFans owner dies aged 43 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/leonid-radvinsky-death-dead-onlyfans-b2943801.html |access-date=March 23, 2026 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

extract: Leonid Saveliyovych Radvinsky (May 30, 1982 – March 20, 2026) was an American billionaire businessman and the majority owner of OnlyFans. Born in the Ukrainian SSR, Radvinsky was the founder of the cam site MyFreeCams (through his holding company, MFCXY, Inc.), and the majority owner of OnlyFans, a content subscription service website, mostly used by pornographic actresses to sell their pornographic content. His website lists his personal investment portfolio. He had an estimated net worth of $4.7 billion at the time of his death, according to Forbes.
